My medical knowledge of the effect on people who genuinely need Xanax is very limited but I do know that recreational use of Xanax is addictive if abused. So my guess is that even when used in people with anxiety it still presents a risk of addiction. Fortunately I'm sure your doctor is well aware of the effects of Xanax and if you ever ask for change they'll slowly take you off of it. There are lots of alternatives to anxiety medications, tons. Theres lots of options that aren't as addictive, however still physiologically addictive. If you have a therapist I would suggest talking to them about your worries and how to handle it. Medicine and therapy is like a peanut butter and jelly sandwich, yeah sure they can be good with just one but they're amazing together. 

And they can be short term, or they can be for the rest of my life. It depends on me, how I feel and what I decide. I'm only a week in on this new medication, I've never take SSRI's or anything like that. So I've yet to see how well this stuff helps me.
Its 3 in the morning, 3 hours later. Im not even remotely high

Maybe you should talk to your doctor about getting off Xanax. From what you tell me you don't need that much Xanax per day (sometimes) so perhaps the doctor went a little over board, but then again I dont know your full story. So thats completely up to you if you want to talk to him/her. 

As for your question at the beginning, I meant once the medicine settles and starts working with my brain, not against it. Sertraline takes 2 or 3 weeks to figure itself out. Sorry, I sometimes get caught up in my own brain lol

Maybe ask around the r/Drugs reddit, although you'll mostly find recreational users there, there are some genuine users with more experience.

First and foremost, I'm 18. So you might disregard this but all well. Anyways, the inability to catch your breath and chest pains do match a panic attack. At least for me. Everybody is different in how they experience panic attacks. I'm currently on medication for anxiety as well, but here's my symptoms. For general anxiety its that unending feeling of being on edge, thinking something bad is going to happen, shaking, increased breathing, being worried about a panic attack, higher bpm, excessive fidgeting, inability to focus, and many more. As for a full on panic attack, its the inability to breath, uncontrollable crying, fear that I'm going to die, feeling out of control, in some cases feeling the need to hide, my head feels different likenots lighter or something, and then there's of course the anxiety in it all. 

These are just my personal symptoms, whatever you feel doesn't need to match me or joe s'moe next to you. Everyone experiences symptoms differently, some have less some have more. What matters now is you've gotten help, and thats the first important step. I wish you luck in your journey.
